resources.string: Every row found in the index is fetched again from the table: the index lacks some of the columns asked for.
SQLite builds a temporary index for this step; none of the table\'s own indexes fits.
Rows found in an index are looked up again in the table, one by one.
SQLite builds a throwaway index while the query runs.
SQLite reports no costs or row estimates, so no step is marked as the heaviest. SCAN reads a whole table or index; SEARCH goes through an index or the rowid.
Estimate only: the statement was planned, not run.
